findings.title: The denial-cache test passes even without the denial cache.
findings.body: The comment says the test grants access "to prove this is not checked", but the code sets `"dashboards:uid:dash1": false`. The cached permissions therefore deny, the fallback goes to the empty `fakeStore`, and that denies too. `resp.Allowed` comes out false whether or not the denial-cache short-circuit exists, so the test checks nothing about it. Set the cached permission to `true` (and/or put the permission in the store) so the test only passes if the denial cache is consulted first.

findings.title: An ambiguous denial cache key lets one resource's denial apply to another.
findings.body: `name` and `parent` are joined with `_`, and both can contain underscores. So different pairs give the same key: for example, name `a_` with parent `b`, and name `a` with parent `_b`, both produce `..._a__b`. A denial cached for one resource then wrongly denies the other until the TTL expires. Use a separator that UIDs can't contain, or escape/length-prefix the parts.
